description: Every afternoon Brassbuckle's first-years build boilers on the long bench in the Polytechnic basement, and none may be lit until a qualified hand has tested it. Lately the qualified hand is you, because Brassbuckle said so in front of the first-years, in a voice that settled the matter. Twelve small boilers stand on the bench in a row. Twelve first-years stand behind them, each certain theirs is the good one.

options.label: Test every boiler properly, valve, seam and gauge, before the bell.

success.text: Nine pass. Two have their safety valves fitted upside down, and you show their builders why that matters with a candle and a great deal of patience. One is perfect, and its builder, a pale boy who has not said a word all afternoon, goes pink to the ears. Brassbuckle has the three best builders pay you a lump each out of their own scuttles, and tells you while they do it about the price of brass when she was a girl.

failure.text: Number seven has a safety valve made, as far as anybody can tell afterwards, from a teaspoon. It lets go while you are bent over it. Brassbuckle carries on with the lesson, which is not about steam, and without breaking her sentence hands you her handkerchief.

options.label: Test them from behind the blast screen, with a long pole and no hurry.

success.text: It takes until the lamps are lit and teaches the first-years mainly about patience. Two boilers fail, harmlessly, at the far end of a pole. Brassbuckle has the first-years find you one lump of coal between their scuttles, on the grounds that you were paid by the hour and most of the hour was pole.

options.label: Let the first-years test their own, and stand where you can catch what goes wrong.

success.text: You teach from the end of the bench. The first-years test their own boilers, nervously at first and then with enthusiasm, and one of them learns what a seam is by having it open in your direction. You take most of it on your apron. Brassbuckle, passing, looks at twelve first-years who can test a boiler and one Tinker with a red hand, and puts your name down for tomorrow as well.
